entities.summary: A neutron star is a celestial body formed when a massive star undergoes a supernova explosion. These cosmic objects are incredibly dense, with the density of a sugar-cube-sized amount of neutron star material weighing about the same as a mountain. The extreme gravity of neutron stars causes them to distort spacetime, making them incredibly dense and hot. The surface temperature of a neutron star can reach millions of degrees Celsius, making it one of the hottest objects in the universe. The discovery of neutron stars has revolutionized our understanding of extreme astrophysics and the behavior of matter under extreme conditions. They are now a crucial area of study in astrophysics, with ongoing research focused on understanding their origins, evolution, and properties.
